MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of the Effective Date set forth on the signature page below, by and between Northbridge Data Systems, Inc., a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 4400 Corridor Parkway, Suite 220, Austin, Texas ("Provider"), and the customer identified on the signature page ("Customer"). Provider and Customer are each referred to individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties."

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Provider offers a hosted inventory-management and point-of-sale software platform, together with related implementation, support, and professional services (collectively, the "Services"); and

WHEREAS, Customer desires to purchase, and Provider desires to provide, the Services on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein, the Parties agree as follows:

1. SERVICES

1.1 Scope. Provider shall make the Services available to Customer as described in one or more order forms executed by the Parties from time to time (each, an "Order Form"), each of which is incorporated into and governed by this Agreement. Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide the Services in a manner consistent with general industry standards.

1.2 Changes. Provider may modify the features and functionality of the Services from time to time, provided that any such modification does not materially reduce the core functionality purchased by Customer under an applicable Order Form during the then-current term.

1.3 Support. Provider shall provide standard support during Provider's normal business hours (Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Central Time, excluding Provider holidays) in accordance with the support tier purchased by Customer.

2. TERM

2.1 Initial Term. This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of twelve (12) months (the "Initial Term"), unless earlier terminated as provided in Section 5.

2.2 Renewal Terms. Following the Initial Term, this Agreement will automatically renew for successive one (1) year terms (each, a "Renewal Term," and together with the Initial Term, the "Term") unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal, provided that Customer's written notice of non-renewal must be received by Provider no later than five (5) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Term, and further provided that the fees payable by Customer for each Renewal Term shall increase by fifteen percent (15%) over the fees in effect during the immediately preceding Term. Provider will post updated pricing on its customer portal but is not obligated to send a separate renewal reminder in advance of the notice deadline.

3. FEES AND PAYMENT

3.1 Fees. Customer shall pay the fees set forth in the applicable Order Form. Except as expressly provided in Section 2.2, fees are exclusive of applicable taxes, which Customer is responsible for paying.

3.2 Invoicing. Provider shall invoice Customer monthly in advance. Payment is due within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. Late payments accrue interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by law.

3.3 Suspension for Nonpayment. Provider may suspend access to the Services if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid more than fifteen (15) days after Provider's written notice of delinquency.

4. CUSTOMER OBLIGATIONS

4.1 Acceptable Use. Customer shall use the Services only for lawful business purposes and in accordance with Provider's then-current acceptable use policy, made available on request.

4.2 Data Accuracy. Customer is solely responsible for the accuracy, quality, and legality of the data Customer uploads or transmits through the Services and for obtaining any rights necessary for Provider to process such data as contemplated by this Agreement.

4.3 Credentials. Customer shall safeguard account credentials issued to its personnel and shall promptly notify Provider of any known or suspected unauthorized use of the Services.

5. TERM AND TERMINATION

5.1 Termination for Cause by Customer. Customer may terminate this Agreement if Provider materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing the breach in reasonable detail.

5.2 Termination by Provider. Provider may terminate this Agreement at any time, for any reason or for no reason, immediately upon written notice to Customer, without any obligation to afford Customer an opportunity to cure and without further liability to Customer of any kind. Upon any termination by Provider under this Section 5.2, Customer remains responsible for all fees accrued through the effective date of termination, and Provider shall have no obligation to refund any prepaid fees.

5.3 Effect of Termination. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason, Customer's right to access the Services immediately ceases, and each Party shall return or destroy the other Party's Confidential Information in accordance with Section 9.

6. INDEMNIFICATION

6.1 Indemnification by Customer. Customer shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Provider from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising out of or in any way related to Customer's use of the Services, Customer's breach of this Agreement, or Customer's violation of any applicable law.

6.2 Cooperation. The Party seeking indemnification shall promptly notify the indemnifying Party of any claim and shall reasonably cooperate, at the indemnifying Party's expense, in the defense of such claim.

7. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

7.1 Disclaimer of Certain Damages. Except for breaches of Section 8 (Confidentiality) or a Party's indemnification obligations, in no event shall either Party be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, including lost profits, arising out of or related to this Agreement, even if advised of the possibility of such damages.

7.2 Liability Cap. Provider's total cumulative liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement, whether in contract, tort, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total fees paid by Customer to Provider during the one (1) month period immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

8. CONFIDENTIALITY

8.1 Definition. "Confidential Information" means any non-public information disclosed by one Party to the other that is designated as confidential or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure.

8.2 Obligations. Each Party shall use the other Party's Confidential Information solely to perform its obligations under this Agreement and shall protect it using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of similar importance, but in no event less than reasonable care.

9. PERSONAL GUARANTEE

9.1 Guarantee. In consideration of Provider entering into this Agreement with Customer, the individual signing this Agreement on behalf of Customer in the signature block below, in his or her individual capacity, personally and unconditionally guarantees the full and prompt payment and performance of all of Customer's obligations under this Agreement, and this guarantee shall remain in full force and effect until all such obligations have been satisfied in full, regardless of any extension, renewal, or modification of this Agreement. The guarantor waives notice of acceptance of this guarantee and any requirement that Provider first pursue collection from Customer before enforcing this guarantee against the guarantor directly.

9.2 Independent Obligation. The obligations of the guarantor under this Section 9 are independent of Customer's obligations, and Provider may pursue the guarantor without first exhausting remedies against Customer.

10. INSURANCE

10.1 Coverage. During the Term, Customer shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with limits of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence, and shall provide Provider with a certificate of insurance upon request.

11. DISPUTE RESOLUTION

11.1 Binding Arbitration. Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively through binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, conducted on an individual basis, and Customer hereby waives any right to participate in a class action, class arbitration, or representative proceeding against Provider, whether as a plaintiff or a class member. The arbitration shall take place in Austin, Texas, and judgment on the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction.

11.2 Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles.

12. GENERAL PROVISIONS

12.1 Assignment. Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that either Party may assign this Agreement in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all of its assets.

12.2 Notices. All notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by email with confirmation of receipt, or by certified mail, to the addresses set forth on the signature page.

12.3 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with all Order Forms, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous agreements, understandings, and communications, whether written or oral.

12.4 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions will continue in full force and effect, and the unenforceable provision will be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable.

12.5 Force Majeure. Neither Party shall be liable for any delay or failure to perform resulting from causes outside its reasonable control, including acts of God, labor disputes, or failures of third-party infrastructure.

12.6 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is deemed an original.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.
